category_title: Struggling readers who view reading as a process of remembering and repeating
minimal_context: The student is in a guided reading group and is asked to read a shared writing journal entry she copied from the board.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Tell me one of the animals from the story.

STUDENT: A dog.

TUTOR: Okay. Now please bring me the shared writing journal entry you copied from the board.

STUDENT: (Brings the journal entry to the teacher.)

TUTOR: Go ahead and read it for me.

STUDENT: The /b/-/a/-/b/-yuh came….

options.A: Redirect the student with comprehension questions about the journal entry, such as, 'What does it seem like the baby wants?'
options.B: Ask the student what she is trying to compose or read in the shared writing journal entry during the guided reading activity.
options.C: Terminate the reading demands and remove the shared writing journal entry materials for 10 seconds during the guided reading group.
options.D: Provide specific phonetic cues (e.g., 'Look at the letters.') and prompt the segmenting and blending of the word and recognition of the sight word.
